patients.summary: A never-smoking high school PE teacher and coach who joined the practice healthy in 2021, developed progressive breathlessness from late 2022, and was found in December 2023 to have alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency with basal bullous emphysema; pulmonology confirmed PiZZ in 2025 and started weekly augmentation in 2026. Mildly raised liver enzymes are being watched.

documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller wants to establish with us. Teaches PE at the high school and coaches; says his old doctor retired and he hasn't had a checkup in a few years. No current issues. Membership info emailed, agreement returned same call. New-patient physical booked 6/22 at 7:40 am so he can get to school after. Asked him to request his old records.

documents.title: New Patient Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
32 y/o M establishing care. Prior PCP retired; last physical roughly 2018 per pt, nothing abnormal that he recalls. Records requested.

No complaints. Runs 3-4 mornings a week, demonstrates drills with his teams, no limitation.

PMH: none. PSH: none. Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
Immunizations: COVID Pfizer x2 this spring (card seen). Tdap unknown date - given today.

Family hx: father had emphysema diagnosed at 42 and died at 48 of cirrhosis, which the family put down to his drinking. Paternal uncle has COPD. Paternal grandmother had cirrhosis, cause never found.

Social: teaches PE at the high school, coaches varsity. Lives with his partner. Never smoked. Alcohol a drink or two a month. No drugs.

ROS negative except as above.

Exam: vitals as charted, BMI ~22. Well-appearing, fit. HEENT normal, no thyromegaly or nodes. Lungs clear to auscultation throughout, good air movement. RRR, no murmur. Abdomen soft, nontender, no hepatosplenomegaly. Skin unremarkable. No edema.

PHQ-2 0.

A/P: Healthy adult, preventive visit.
- CBC, CMP, lipid panel; one-time HIV and hep C screen
- Tdap today
- Flu shot this fall
- Family hx of early emphysema in a drinker father noted; he has no symptoms. Revisit if anything changes.
RTC 1 yr.

documents.title: Office Visit - Dyspnea
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Declan comes in about his breathing. Says it started creeping up a little over a year ago, around October of last year, and has slowly gotten worse. Now one flight of stairs leaves him winded, and a few minutes of walking fast does the same. Tired more than he used to be. At work he's stopped demonstrating drills for the kids and just talks them through it, which bothers him. Dry cough, mild, most days. Some wheezing now and then, mostly with exertion. No fever, no chest pain, no leg swelling, no hemoptysis. No orthopnea.

Never smoked. His partner started smoking again over a year ago and does smoke in the house. Drinks rarely. No work exposures he can think of beyond gym dust.

Family: father with emphysema at 42 who died of cirrhosis at 48; paternal uncle with COPD; paternal grandmother with cirrhosis of unknown cause.

Meds none. NKDA.

Exam: T 36.8, HR 82, RR 18, BP 122/78, SpO2 91% RA. Weight down about 3 kg from last summer's physical. Not in distress at rest. Scattered end-expiratory wheezes, rhonchi at both bases. Heart regular, no murmur. No JVD. Abdomen soft, no liver edge. No clubbing, no edema.

A/P: 34 y/o never smoker with 14 months of progressive exertional dyspnea, cough, wheeze, and a resting sat of 91%. With his father's early emphysema and two relatives with liver disease, I am worried about alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency.
- CXR PA/lat today, walked over to imaging
- Serum alpha-1 antitrypsin level, CBC, CMP drawn here
- Full PFTs with lung volumes and DLCO, ordered
- Will call him when PFTs are back to put it together

Addendum 15:40: CXR reviewed - hyperlucent lungs, bullous change at both bases. Fits the concern above. Pt aware by phone, PFTs set for 12/12.

documents.title: Blood test result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Declan, your alpha-1 antitrypsin level came back low at 24 (normal is roughly 100 to 190). Your blood count and the kidney and liver tests were fine. A low level like this goes along with what the X-ray showed. I'd like the breathing tests on Tuesday before we talk through what it means - I'll call you once I have them.

documents.title: RE: Blood test result
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Ok. I looked it up, is this the thing that runs in families? My dad's lungs were bad young. Talk Tuesday.

reports.text: PULMONARY FUNCTION LABORATORY REPORT. Referring: primary care. Tests performed: spirometry with pre and post bronchodilator, lung volumes by plethysmography, single-breath diffusing capacity. Effort and reproducibility acceptable. Interpretation: Obstructive ventilatory defect. Diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide is decreased. Results tables attached to the original report.
reports.conclusion: Obstructive ventilatory pattern with decreased DLCO.

documents.title: Pulmonary function test report
documents.author: pulmonary function lab
documents.body: Hospital pulmonary function laboratory. Date of test: 12/12/2023. Patient: Declan Merrill, DOB 05/09/1989. Allergies: NKDA. Obstructive ventilatory defect with decreased diffusing capacity. Interpreting physician signature on file. Received electronically, routed to PCP.

orders.reason: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency with basal bullous changes and obstruction

documents.title: Results discussion
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Called pt at lunch, ~20 min. Went over the pieces: basal bullous change on CXR, obstruction with a low DLCO on yesterday's PFTs, AAT level 24, in a 34-year-old who has never smoked and whose father had emphysema at 42. This is alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency affecting his lungs. Explained it is inherited and that the exact type is worked out with genetic testing, which pulmonology will handle along with the question of treatment.

Referral to pulmonology placed, marked soon.
Asked that his partner not smoke in the house or the car at all - he says she's already offered to take it outside. Keep drinking to a minimum, liver can be involved in this condition too. Flu and COVID already done this fall.
He asked about his school duties - fine to keep teaching and coaching, pace himself, no need to push through breathlessness.
He'll let me know when pulmonology calls.

documents.title: Referral processed
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pulmonology referral faxed with the 12/5 note, CXR, AAT result and PFT report. Their office scheduled him for 2/6/24. Pt notified by portal. Insurance does not require a referral number for this plan.

documents.body: Just closing the loop - I saw pulmonology back on Feb 6. They did more breathing tests, didn't start me on anything, and want to see me again in about a year and a half unless it gets worse. Did they send you anything?

documents.title: RE: Saw the lung doctor
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for telling me - nothing has come over yet. We'll ask them for the note. Keep me posted on how you're doing in the meantime.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
35M, physical. Problem: alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency, dx 12/2023.

Breathing about where it was last winter - stairs still wind him, he paces himself at practice. Cough comes and goes. Saw pulmonology 2/2024, no treatment started, next visit planned for fall 2025; their note never reached us despite two requests. Partner smokes outside only now.

Meds none. NKDA. Alcohol: a drink or two a month.

Exam: vitals as charted, SpO2 93% RA. Thin, comfortable at rest. Breath sounds mildly diminished both sides, no wheeze today, no crackles. Heart regular. Abdomen soft, no hepatomegaly. No clubbing or edema.

PHQ-2 0.

A/P:
- AATD with lung involvement: stable by history. Keep the pulmonology follow-up. Pneumococcal vaccine today given chronic lung disease.
- Preventive: CBC, CMP, lipids. Flu and updated COVID today.
RTC 1 yr.

documents.title: Lab results

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
36M here before the school year. AATD, lung involvement.

Thinks the breathing has slipped over the past year. Gave up jogging this spring, gets tired and tight in the chest if he tries. Stairs at school slower than the other teachers. Still coaching, delegates more of the running to his assistant. Cough unchanged. Partner keeps her smoking outdoors, away from him. Pulmonology follow-up booked for 10/20.

No meds. NKDA.

Exam: SpO2 92% RA, other vitals as charted. Weight 67 kg, down a few kg over two years. Thin, speaks full sentences. Diminished breath sounds throughout, prolonged expiratory phase, no wheeze. Heart regular. Abdomen soft. No clubbing, no edema.

PHQ-2 1 - says it's frustrating not to keep up with the kids, mood otherwise fine.

A/P:
- AATD: gradual worsening by history and sat. Glad he's seeing pulmonology in October; asked him to make sure they send us the note this time.
- CBC, BMP.
- Flu and COVID in October at a nurse visit.
RTC 1 yr, sooner after pulmonology.

documents.title: Pulmonology follow-up letter with addendum
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
PULMONARY MEDICINE CLINIC - FOLLOW-UP NOTE
Date of service: 10/20/2025
Re: Declan Merrill, DOB 05/09/1989
Allergies: NKDA
Medications: none

Mr. Merrill is seen in follow-up for alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency. Over roughly three years his breathing has steadily declined. He now falls behind colleagues on the school stairs and has given up jogging because it brings on fatigue and a tight chest. No daily medicines. Lifelong nonsmoker; he reports no current secondhand smoke and no occupational exposures. Alcohol occasional, no drug use. Father had early lung disease and died at 48 of cirrhosis that was attributed to alcohol.

Exam: SpO2 93% on room air. Thin man, mildly tachypneic at rest. Breath sounds diminished bilaterally with a prolonged expiratory phase. Hyperresonant to percussion, AP diameter mildly increased. No wheezes or rales. No digital clubbing.

Data: Today's chest film shows bilateral hyperinflation with bullae at the bases. PFTs today: obstruction, increased TLC, residual volume markedly increased. Hepatic panel: ALT 62, AST 47, mildly elevated. Serum AAT 22 mg/dL, consistent with deficiency.

Impression: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency with progressive obstructive lung disease and mildly raised transaminases.
Plan: SERPINA1 genotyping sent today. We will contact him with results and discuss augmentation.

ADDENDUM 11/06/2025: Genotype returned homozygous Z (PiZZ), the most severe deficiency variant. Discussed by phone. Recommended he consider weekly IV augmentation therapy; he is interested and we will submit to his insurer. Advised avoiding further liver and lung injury: minimize or stop alcohol, avoid hepatotoxic medicines and supplements, avoid smoke exposure, keep vaccines current. Suggest PCP follow liver enzymes.

Received by fax 11/24/2025 after records request.

orders.reason: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency with elevated transaminases

documents.title: Office Visit - AATD follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here to go over the pulmonology letter (10/20 visit, 11/6 addendum; arrived 11/24).

Summary of their findings: SpO2 93%, hyperinflation with basilar bullae on CXR, PFTs obstructive with increased TLC and markedly increased RV, AAT 22, genotype PiZZ. ALT 62 / AST 47. They recommend weekly augmentation and are working on insurance approval.

He's absorbing the ZZ result. Breathing unchanged since August. Asks what the liver part means. No jaundice, itching, abdominal swelling or dark urine. Alcohol 1-2 a month; he's willing to stop. No supplements, no regular acetaminophen or NSAIDs.

Exam: SpO2 93% RA, vitals otherwise as charted. Thin. Diminished breath sounds, prolonged expiration, no wheeze. Abdomen soft, nontender, no hepatomegaly or splenomegaly. No jaundice. No edema.

A/P:
1. AATD, PiZZ, lung disease: augmentation per pulmonology. He'll tell me when it starts.
2. Elevated liver enzymes, mild, in AATD: repeat hepatic panel today. Abdominal ultrasound. Advised stopping alcohol and checking with me before any new medicine or supplement.
3. Hepatitis A dose 1 and Heplisav-B dose 1 today. Heplisav #2 in a month (nurse visit), hep A #2 in 6+ months.
See me in spring.

reports.text: ULTRASOUND ABDOMEN COMPLETE. Indication: alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency, mildly elevated transaminases. Liver normal in size with normal echotexture and smooth contour. No focal hepatic lesion. Hepatic and portal veins patent with normal flow direction. Gallbladder without stones or wall thickening. Common bile duct normal caliber. Pancreas visualized portions unremarkable. Spleen normal in size. Kidneys normal in size without hydronephrosis. No ascites.

documents.title: Ultrasound and liver tests
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your ultrasound looks normal - the liver is a normal size and texture, with no spots or fluid. The liver enzymes from the 9th were still a little up (ALT 59, AST 43), about the same as pulmonology found. We'll recheck at your spring visit. Enjoy the break.

documents.title: Immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Heplisav-B dose 2 of 2, 0.5 mL IM L deltoid. Hep B series complete. Reminded him hep A dose 2 is due June or later. No reaction during observation.

documents.title: Started infusions
documents.author: patient
documents.body: FYI insurance approved it and I had my first infusion last Tuesday (2/3) at the infusion center pulmonology uses. It's once a week, about an hour. Second one today went fine. No side effects so far.

documents.title: RE: Started infusions
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Great news, thanks for telling me. Let us know if you have any fevers, rash or other reactions after an infusion. We'll talk about it in April.

documents.title: Office Visit - AATD follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up. On weekly alpha-1 proteinase inhibitor infusions since 2/3, run by pulmonology at their infusion center; nothing from them in writing about it yet. Tolerating it well, no reactions. Breathing no worse than December, no better either. Cough the same.

Meds: alpha-1 proteinase inhibitor 60 mg/kg IV weekly (pulmonology) - added to list today. NKDA.

Exam: SpO2 93% RA, vitals otherwise as charted. Thin, comfortable. Diminished breath sounds, prolonged expiration, no wheeze or crackles. Abdomen soft, no organomegaly. No edema.

A/P:
1. AATD, PiZZ: on augmentation via pulmonology.
2. Mildly elevated liver enzymes with normal ultrasound: hepatic panel today.
3. Hep A #2 due June or later - nurse visit then, or at the September physical.
Physical in September.

documents.title: Liver tests
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Liver enzymes are about where they've been (ALT 64, AST 46), mildly up and not climbing in any worrying way. Bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase normal. We'll keep checking a couple of times a year.

documents.title: September physical
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Can I get my physical on the calendar for early September? Mornings before 8 are best. And I can get the second hep A shot then if that's easier.

documents.title: RE: September physical
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: You're booked Thursday 9/10 at 7:40 am. We've noted the hep A dose for that visit.
